**2.** ANOVA ($F$ test) — one numerical response (live-watch time) compared across four independent groups, so a many-means comparison rather than repeated two-sample tests.

**4.** $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \cdots = \mu_8,$ the average chance quality is the same across the eight play patterns; $H_A:$ at least one mean differs. p-value $= 91/1000 = 0.091 > 0.05;$ fail to reject $H_0$ — no convincing evidence that average chance quality differs by play pattern at the 2025 Women's Euro. Observational data, so even a rejection would have licensed association only.

**6.** (a) $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \mu_3 = \mu_4 = \mu_5,$ the average certification score is the same for all five formats; $H_A:$ at least one format's mean differs. (b) $df_G = 5 - 1 = 4$ and $df_E = 45 - 5 = 40.$ (c) p-value $= 0.0168 < 0.05;$ reject $H_0$ — the average certification score differs for at least one pair of teaching formats.

**8.** $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \cdots = \mu_8,$ average audit score equal across the eight sub-networks; $H_A:$ at least one differs. Conditions: independence must be assumed (reports within a sub-network share a senior scout); normality workable given the group sizes; constant variance questionable (SDs $3.43$ to $9.32,$ ratio near 3, with uneven group sizes), so proceed with caution. $MSG = 525.01/7 = 75.00,$ $MSE = 7584.11/189 = 40.13,$ $F_{7,189} = 1.87,$ p-value $= 0.0767 > 0.05;$ fail to reject $H_0$ — no convincing evidence that average audit quality differs across sub-networks.

**10.** (a) $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \cdots = \mu_8,$ the average chance quality is the same across the eight play patterns at the 2022 Men's World Cup; $H_A:$ at least one mean differs. (b) Independence: shots cluster within matches and moves, so it must be assumed (observational data); normality: xG is strongly right-skewed, but the group sizes (smallest 17 and 21) make this workable with caution; constant variance: SDs run $0.091$ to $0.157,$ reasonably met. (c) $MSG = 0.3795/7 = 0.0542,$ $MSE = 21.2877/1418 = 0.0150,$ $F_{7,1418} = 3.61,$ p-value $= 0.0007 < 0.05;$ reject $H_0$ — average chance quality differs across play patterns here, the opposite verdict to the Euro's Exercise 4, so the pattern (counters on top at $0.159$) is tournament-specific, not a universal law.

**12.** (a) False — rejecting $H_0$ says only that at least one mean differs. (b) True. (c) False — the corrected pairwise tests may find no single pair discernibly different. (d) False — four groups give $\binom{4}{2} = 6$ comparisons, so $\alpha^\star = 0.05/6 \approx 0.0083.$

**14.** (a) $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = \cdots = \mu_5,$ average weekly video-review hours are equal across the five experience bands; $H_A:$ at least one band's mean differs. (b) $F_{4,900} = 8.04,$ p-value $= 2.3 \times 10^{-6} < 0.05;$ reject $H_0$ — average weekly video-review hours differ across experience bands.
